# OmniDataEditor 0.1.0

The first release of OmniDataEditor brings a framework independent TypeScript editing engine to applications that already have their own tables, forms and persistence APIs. Use it to add consistent entity editing without replacing the interface around it.

## Try the playground

Explore the [interactive team directory](https://bensitu.github.io/omni-data-editor/examples/showcase/): edit a person in a dialog, change a salary inline, update several people together, and search for an office asynchronously. The demo runs entirely in the browser with sample data that resets on reload.

The [documentation](https://bensitu.github.io/omni-data-editor/) includes integration guides, focused examples and an API reference.

## One editing model, several interfaces

- **Keep edits separate from saved data.** Immutable drafts let an application validate and review changes before committing them.
- **Connect your own persistence.** Typed persistence results distinguish accepted changes, validation errors, conflicts and uncertain outcomes. Applications supply their server calls and concurrency preconditions.
- **Choose where editing happens.** Use native dialogs, anchored inline controls or the headless engine with a custom interface. DataTables and Tabulator adapters connect existing tables to the same editing model.
- **Handle more than one entity.** Batch editing reports individual outcomes and preserves successful updates when another entity needs attention.
- **Extend the controls.** Native field renderers, cancellable asynchronous selection and explicit CSS imports keep presentation configurable.

## Install

After the npm packages are published, install the common entry point and its optional default stylesheet:

```sh
pnpm add @omnidataeditor/editor @omnidataeditor/theme-default
```

```ts
import { createEditor, textField, dialog } from '@omnidataeditor/editor';
import '@omnidataeditor/theme-default/styles.css';

type Person = { id: number; name: string };
const fields = [textField<Person>('name', { label: 'Name', required: true })];
const editor = createEditor<Person>({
  fields,
  identity: (entity) => entity.id,
  persistence: {
    async update({ candidate }) {
      return { ok: true, entity: candidate };
    },
  },
});

editor.use(dialog({ fields, title: 'Edit person' }));
editor.edit({ id: 1, name: 'Ada' });
```

This example accepts changes in memory. Connect the persistence port to your application API to save changes on a server.

## Packages

All nine packages share version **0.1.0** and use ESM exports.

| Package                               | Purpose                                                                            |
| ------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `@omnidataeditor/editor`              | Common factories and type exports                                                  |
| `@omnidataeditor/core`                | Headless editing, validation, persistence and conflicts; zero runtime dependencies |
| `@omnidataeditor/dom`                 | Native field controls, forms and renderer contracts                                |
| `@omnidataeditor/presentation-dialog` | Native modal presentation                                                          |
| `@omnidataeditor/presentation-inline` | Anchored inline presentation                                                       |
| `@omnidataeditor/host-datatables`     | DataTables integration                                                             |
| `@omnidataeditor/host-tabulator`      | Tabulator integration                                                              |
| `@omnidataeditor/field-async-select`  | Cancellable asynchronous selection                                                 |
| `@omnidataeditor/theme-default`       | Optional styles and theme properties                                               |

Host adapters and asynchronous selection are optional. Import `@omnidataeditor/core` on its own for headless integrations. JavaScript entry points are safe to import in Node and server bundles; rendering controls requires a browser.

## Release downloads and compatibility

The assets contain the nine original package archives, `SHA256SUMS` and `release-manifest.json`. The manifest identifies the source commit and package integrity values. npm publication is a separate manual workflow that publishes these same archives; GitHub release publication alone does not make the packages available on npm.

This is a **0.x** release: public interfaces may change between minor versions. Review the [compatibility guidance](https://bensitu.github.io/omni-data-editor/support), [accessibility requirements](https://bensitu.github.io/omni-data-editor/accessibility) and [security guidance](https://bensitu.github.io/omni-data-editor/security) when integrating the library.
